strengths: The paper identifies a concrete and practically relevant failure mode in modern text-to-image models: prompts whose concepts are not logically inconsistent but conflict with learned visual priors, such as a dragon blowing water or a butterfly in a bee hive. The framing of contextual contradiction is clear and useful for analyzing compositional failures beyond standard attribute binding.

The proposed Stage-Aware Prompting method is simple, training-free, and well motivated by the coarse-to-fine behavior of diffusion denoising. Using proxy prompts at different denoising stages is an intuitive mechanism that can plausibly preserve early layout while deferring conflicting identity/detail cues.

The paper provides consistent empirical support across several settings. SAP improves GPT-4o alignment over FLUX from 44.3 to 62.13 on Whoops-Hard and from 57.16 to 66.16 on ContraBench, and also improves SD3.0. The user study reports strong preference for SAP in both alignment and quality against multiple baselines.

The ablations are helpful: removing in-context examples or reasoning substantially reduces performance, limiting to two proxies is close but weaker, and perturbing timestep boundaries shows the method depends on the approximate denoising stage rather than exact step values.

Qualitative examples are compelling and illustrate the claimed mechanism well. The appendix includes prompt lists, the LLM instruction, VLM evaluation prompt, alternative LLM results, non-contradictory prompt checks, and failure analysis, which improves transparency.
weaknesses: The evaluation relies heavily on GPT-4o both as the prompt decomposer and as the VLM judge. This creates a potential methodological coupling: the same model family may reward decompositions and semantic interpretations that match its own priors. The user study helps, but it is limited to 24 prompts and lacks statistical uncertainty or detailed protocol information.

The new benchmarks are small and partly curated with ChatGPT-generated candidates. ContraBench has only 40 prompts, and Whoops-Hard is a selected subset of 100 prompts. This makes it hard to assess generalization to broader prompt distributions or to know whether the method is tuned to the kinds of contradictions represented in the examples.

The method’s novelty is moderate. Time-varying or multi-prompt conditioning and LLM-guided prompt planning are already present in related work. The contribution is mainly the specific application to contextual contradictions plus stage-aware proxy construction, which is useful but not a major algorithmic advance.

Fairness of comparisons is somewhat uneven because baselines use different backbones or implementations, including SD3, FLUX, FLUX-schnell, SD1.5-based Ella, and reimplemented R2F on FLUX. Some reported failures may reflect backbone or implementation mismatch rather than the core baseline idea.

The approach depends on proprietary GPT-4o for the main results and on hand-designed in-context examples. Although a Llama-3.1-8B result is included, it is notably weaker on Whoops and ContraBench, so reproducibility and deployment without closed models remain concerns.

The method can fail when the LLM chooses poor proxies or when the base diffusion model cannot express quantities, orientations, symbolic details, or unusual structures. The failure analysis is honest, but proxy assignment accounts for most failures, indicating that the central automatic decomposition step is still brittle.

The definition of contextual contradiction is conceptually appealing but operationally loose. The paper does not provide an automatic or rigorous way to determine whether a prompt contains such a contradiction, so benchmark construction and success criteria remain somewhat subjective.

strengths: The paper identifies a real and practically relevant failure mode in text-to-image generation: prompts whose requested composition conflicts with strong learned priors, such as unusual objects, actions, contexts, or identities.
weaknesses: The core method is technically simple and only moderately original: it combines LLM-generated prompt rewriting with timestep-dependent prompt switching, both of which are close to existing multi-prompt and LLM-guided diffusion techniques. The paper does not convincingly isolate what is new beyond applying these ingredients to a curated contradiction setting.

The empirical evidence is not strong enough for the breadth of the claims. The main quantitative evaluation relies on GPT-4o as the judge while GPT-4o is also used to generate the method's prompt decompositions, creating a concerning dependency between the controller and evaluator.

The new benchmarks are small and heavily curated: ContraBench has only 40 prompts generated by ChatGPT and human-filtered, and Whoops-Hard is a selected subset of 100 prompts. The paper gives limited detail about filtering criteria, annotator agreement, prompt selection bias, or whether prompts overlap stylistically with the in-context examples.

The user study is under-specified. It reports win rates from 61 users and 24 prompts, but does not provide confidence intervals, statistical tests, per-baseline sample counts, interface details, randomization protocol, or whether participants were blinded to method identity.

Several baselines appear difficult to interpret. For example, R2F on FLUX performs far worse than the base FLUX model, suggesting possible implementation or hyperparameter mismatch. This weakens the conclusion that SAP is broadly superior to prior prompt scheduling methods.

Ablations support that prompt decomposition matters, but they do not fully separate the effects of LLM rewriting, manual/in-context prompt engineering, concept substitution, and stage scheduling. A stronger comparison to static LLM-rewritten prompts and alternative scheduling heuristics would be important.

The method depends substantially on proprietary or variable LLM behavior. Although a Llama-3.1 result is included, performance drops and reproducibility remains limited unless the exact prompts, decoding settings, generated decompositions, seeds, and code are released.

Failure analysis suggests many errors are due to incorrect proxy assignment, which is central to the proposed method rather than merely an external limitation. The paper frames this as an LLM limitation, but the method's success depends on that component being reliable.

The qualitative examples are visually compelling, but many are selected cases where the intended proxy path is intuitive. The paper does not sufficiently analyze harder categories where substitution is ambiguous, culturally dependent, logically precise, or requires exact counting/spatial relations.

strengths: The paper identifies a meaningful and underexplored failure mode in text-to-image generation: prompts whose concepts are not logically contradictory but conflict with learned visual priors, such as dragons blowing water or butterflies in beehives. The framing is clear and useful for the community.

The proposed Stage-Aware Prompting method is simple, training-free, and well matched to the coarse-to-fine behavior of diffusion denoising. Using proxy prompts early for layout/pose and switching to the target prompt later is technically plausible and well illustrated.

The empirical evidence is fairly strong. SAP improves over FLUX, SD3.0, R2F, Annealing Guidance, Ella, and VL-DNP on Whoops, Whoops-Hard, and ContraBench, with notable gains on harder settings such as Whoops-Hard and ContraBench. The qualitative examples also support the claimed failure mode and improvement.

The paper includes useful ablations: removing in-context examples, removing explanations, limiting proxy count, perturbing timestep boundaries, comparing GPT-4o with Llama-3.1-8B, and testing non-contradictory PartiPrompts-Simple prompts. These make the method’s behavior more credible.
The user study is a valuable complement to GPT-4o evaluation, since visual quality and subtle semantic alignment are difficult to capture with automated metrics alone.
The appendix improves reproducibility by listing the LLM instruction, in-context examples, evaluation prompt, ContraBench prompts, and Whoops-Hard prompt subset.
weaknesses: The benchmark construction raises some concern. ContraBench is small, curated with ChatGPT candidates and human filtering, and many examples appear close in spirit to the manually designed in-context decomposition examples. This makes it hard to judge generalization to a broader natural distribution of contradictory prompts.

The main quantitative evaluator is GPT-4o, while GPT-4o is also used to generate decompositions in the primary method. Even though the evaluation is visual and a Llama ablation is included, relying heavily on the same proprietary model family for method and metric may introduce bias or make the absolute scores difficult to interpret.

The method’s novelty is moderate. Prompt switching over denoising stages and LLM-based prompt decomposition both connect closely to prior multi-prompt and LLM-guided diffusion work. The contribution is a compelling combination targeted at contextual contradictions, rather than a fundamentally new generative mechanism.

The paper does not fully quantify the robustness of LLM decomposition quality. The failure analysis says most failures come from proxy assignment, but the study would be stronger with systematic measurements of invalid decompositions, parsing failures, variance across LLM samples, and sensitivity to the 20 in-context examples.

The user study lacks some details needed to assess statistical reliability, such as participant screening, randomization/blinding protocol, confidence intervals, and per-baseline significance testing.

Reproducibility is limited by dependence on proprietary GPT-4o for the strongest results and by the absence, in the manuscript, of complete implementation details such as exact FLUX/SD3 settings, seeds, decoding parameters, and whether generated images and code will be released.

Some claims are broader than the evidence supports. The method is demonstrated on curated contradictory prompts, but it remains unclear how often contextual contradictions occur in ordinary user prompts and how reliably SAP detects when no decomposition is needed beyond the simple PartiPrompts-Simple check.
